runners_data.name: Thyer

runners_data.name: Calm The Jets

runners_data.name: Liberate

runners_data.name: Albion Power

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: W J Lee rides this 3yo prominent racer who won at 7f on Tapeta and placed on Good; stepping back to 1m, Good ground (only 2/5 runs), and a form figure of -96 most recently suggests he is below his best — Good Tapeta winner reverting to turf is a risk.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan's mount is an uncertain style (U) 3yo for W McCreery with a visor; four consecutive runs on Good all at this course with two placed efforts suggest course form is genuine — needs traffic to clear to get involved from a likely midfield-to-rear position.

races.paceDynamic: No More Porter is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-horse field and, with no serious challenger disputing the lead, is set to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo on Good ground over a mile at the Curragh. The real story is in the prominent ranks: Tachos, Therewillbeglory, Calm The Jets, Chester Nimitz, Highbury See See, Majestic King, Neo Smart, Nautic Star, and Liberation Date all want to race in the first three or four lengths, creating a densely congested early order that will compress runners into a tight band through the middle stages and generate traffic problems two to three furlongs out. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Tofino, Usuario Amigo, Liberate, and Albion Power are unlikely to secure their natural positions and will effectively race out of role, blunting their effectiveness. With a moderate, uncontested gallop set by No More Porter and a wall of prominent runners fighting for space, this race shape decisively favours horses who can travel prominently within the first half-dozen and produce a sustained finish off a sound pace — patient prominent-to-midfield types with a proven turn of foot on Good ground are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Grind It Out

scenarios.body: If the nine prominent runners race in a compressed bunch behind No More Porter and the pace remains honest but not punishing, producing a test of finishing quality from the front half.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes significant interference two to three furlongs out, blocking and checking runners in the midfield group and opening a gap for one horse to dart through.
scenarios.body: If the prominent congestion causes significant interference two to three furlongs out, blocking and checking runners in the midfield group and opening a gap for one horse to dart through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Pinches It
scenarios.trigger: If No More Porter dictates fully unchallenged and the prominent pack becomes so preoccupied with each other that the pace is effectively stolen at the front.
scenarios.body: If No More Porter dictates fully unchallenged and the prominent pack becomes so preoccupied with each other that the pace is effectively stolen at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion burns out the front-half runners in the closing stages and genuine hold-up horses are able to find clear passage late.
scenarios.body: If the prominent congestion burns out the front-half runners in the closing stages and genuine hold-up horses are able to find clear passage late.

watchPoints.text: Traffic flashpoint 2-3f out: with nine prominent runners — Tachos, Therewillbeglory, Calm The Jets, Chester Nimitz, Highbury See See, Majestic King, Neo Smart, Nautic Star and Liberation Date — all hunting the same handful of positions, a serious interference incident on the final bend is a genuine risk that could end several horses' chances abruptly.

No More Porter's tempo is critical: if Adam Caffrey is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged and the prominent pack becomes distracted by each other, the front-runner could steal a march that the 22-horse field cannot collectively close — watch the early splits carefully.

Majestic King is flagged as fading in the finish despite Oisin Murphy riding; if he races prominently and hits the front before the furlong pole, he may be vulnerable to challengers late — watch his position from 2f out.

Calm The Jets carries the same fade flag and a prominent style — if Rory Cleary sends him forward early to get cover, he could briefly look like a threat before flattening inside the final furlong, potentially causing interference as the pack hits him.

Prevalence (Colin Keane, OR 82, G M Lyons) is the classiest horse in the field on raw ratings but has only four career runs — watch whether Keane opts to hold him up through the traffic or commit earlier than usual given the congestion risk.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson

runners_data.name: Una Matata

runners_data.name: Apache Outlaw

races.paceDynamic: Alfred Tennyson is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to contest the lead, he should dictate from the front at a sustainable, unforced gallop over this flat Curragh 7f. With just one horse setting the pace, the tempo is unlikely to be brutal, meaning the lead and prominent positions carry a structural advantage — those tracking Alfred Tennyson within the first three or four lengths are best placed to kick at the two-furlong pole without burning reserves chasing a fast pace. The field holds significantly more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Arryaaf, Indigo Dream, Spacebound, Collecting Coin, Little Empire, and Gypsy Queen are all natural prominent racers, but with only one confirmed leader, most will be shuffled back against their instincts, crowding the midfield pack. Summer Island and Una Matata — genuine prominent types — are most likely to push through and secure early positions alongside Alfred Tennyson, while true hold-up runners Smoke Them Out, Apache Outlaw, and Thru And Thru will find themselves further back than ideal. The tactical verdict is clear: a single-paced, uncontested gallop strongly favours horses with a prominent or close-tracking style who can stride into contention without needing a strong pace to reel in; closers and hold-up horses face a difficult task if the tempo does not truly accelerate.

watchPoints.text: Alfred Tennyson holds a massive structural advantage as the only horse guaranteed a clear lead — watch whether Chris Hayes exploits the uncontested gallop to dictate terms completely and save enough for the final furlong at 7f, a trip longer than his recent sprinting assignments.

With 18 runners and a large cluster of prominent types all seeking the same positions in the first quarter-mile, watch for early positional bunching and potential interference — horses drawn widest will face a particularly difficult task getting into contention without expending energy.

Summer Island and Una Matata are both natural prominent racers redistributed to midfield on the map — watch at the start whether Oisin Murphy (Summer Island) or McDonogh (Una Matata) immediately push forward to reclaim their natural positions, as this would intensify early pace pressure on Alfred Tennyson.

Invincible Will is the most credible hold-up threat if any pace develops — watch whether Jack Kearney (3lb claim) can position him just off midfield on the inner to get a clear run in the final two furlongs, as the horse has won twice on Good at this exact trip.

races.paceDynamic: Quatre Bras is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 1m4f on Good ground at the Curragh — a flat track that rewards those who travel well through the race rather than those who need a strong pace to close into. With no genuine rival pressing Quatre Bras for the lead, the tempo is likely to be controlled and honest rather than truly searching, which compresses the advantage for deep closers and places a premium on horses who can sit handy and quicken. The field is packed with horses whose natural position is prominent or hold-up, and because not all of them can achieve their preferred berth, several — including Tassarolo, Folly Beach, Granville Street, Cracking Cloud, and Kool One — will be shuffled further back than ideal, creating a falsely compressed midfield group. In a race where the pace is controlled and the rail is not a significant bias factor on Good ground, horses racing prominently or in the first half of the field and possessing a genuine finishing kick will be best placed; deep hold-up horses racing well off the tempo in a race not run to suit them are at a structural disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Quatre Bras — watch if it is allowed to dominate entirely unchallenged; a controlled solo lead over 1m4f on flat Good ground could carry it much further into the finish than its poor recent form (204088) suggests.

Tatum and Kool One are the two prominent horses with the clearest distance credentials at 1m4f Good — if either gets a clear run tracking Quatre Bras, they become the primary dangers in the principal scenario.

Derry Lad ran just two days ago — monitor its market position; a horse with a fades-in-finish flag and a 2-day turnaround in a 23-runner field is a significant risk of early withdrawals or non-competing behaviour.

Nod Of Approval finished second over 1m4f at the Curragh on Good earlier this season — the most directly relevant piece of form in the field — and is worth tracking in-running from a hold-up position if it gets a clean passage in the straight.

With at least five horses tagged as redistributed (Tassarolo, Folly Beach, Faro Island, Royal Alliance, Covert Legend, Derry Lad), watch for significant early crowding as genuine prominent types attempt to reclaim their natural positions from wide draws — incidents in the first two furlongs are elevated in probability.

runners_data.name: Poetic Sound
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter with a clear path to the front; Colin Keane's booking is significant, her recent win at 14f on good ground confirms current form, but her style_fit flag reminds that she is racing somewhat out of role at the head of affairs — if she is reeled in, she may not find as much as hoped.

runners_data.name: The Shunter
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old returning after a 236-day absence for Emmet Mullins, whose 14-day strike rate of 2/7 is modest; hurdling headgear suggests stamina is not in doubt but the lengthy absence and declining profile at this level make a bold showing hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Delta
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides a lightly framed 4-year-old for Joseph O'Brien who has solid course form at Good going (1W3P in five sim-going runs) and a versatile front-to-mid trip profile; tongue-tie fitted, represents the most credible prominent-tracking threat to the pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Kilmeaden
runners_data.note: Donnacha/Aidan O'Brien yard runner with a big-field handicap win at 16f at HEA and subsequent placed efforts over staying trips; 5lb claimer Paddy Harnett reduces the weight burden, and his good-ground record (5/13, 1W3P) makes this surface no worry — a genuine player from a close tracking position.

runners_data.name: Reverend Hubert
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up specialist with two wins at 18-25f on good ground in recent history and sound stamina credentials; C Byrnes' stable has a quiet 14-day record (0/11), but this is Hubert's true style and he is the most authentic closer in the field.

runners_data.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for W P Mullins, but the form string of 2030-6 shows no wins on good ground (0W3P in five sim-going runs) and last-time-out sixth at 14f on good is uninspiring; has a natural prominent style but lacks the finishing punch to trouble the leaders.

runners_data.name: Highwind
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners another W P Mullins representative; a true hold-up type (headgear: p) who is 0W1P across 14 good-ground outings in the profile, suggesting he rarely wins in this style-scenario — needs a stronger early pace than this race is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Ballyadam
runners_data.note: A prolific course-winner (1/16f/GOO most recently) whose true nature is to race prominently, though the field's pace density means he is mapped to midfield; Henry De Bromhead's yard is active (T14: 11/38) and Ronan Whelan knows this horse — the question is whether he can recover from his displaced running style.

runners_data.name: Robbies Rock
runners_data.note: Three wins on good ground and a course of recent prominent-race form, but a finishing 20th and 8th in his last two starts at this distance range casts doubt; Robert Whearty rides and the style_fit flag confirms he is unlikely to dominate from his natural spot — his chance hinges on getting a position he probably cannot secure.

runners_data.name: Happy Jacky
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old veteran returning after 288 days (32 days since a jump start), with four wins on good ground over extreme distances; Gavin Ryan takes the ride for a yard with a decent recent record, but age, layoff and redistributed style all work against him securing his natural prominent spot.

runners_data.name: Cock And Bull
runners_data.note: Off the track for 272 days (73 days since a jump run) for Emmet Mullins, whose 14-day record here is 0/8; the form in flat handicaps is uninspiring (never higher than fifth in five profile runs) and the long absence makes this a speculative runner — authentic hold-up style but lacks the rating and form to capitalise.

runners_data.name: Hatim
runners_data.note: French-trained 4-year-old (F Rohaut, T14: 0/7) returning after 227 days with a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag and only soft-ground form in the profile; 0W in two handicap runs, limited stamina under pressure, and the trip looks too demanding for a horse who doesn't see it out on easier ground.

runners_data.name: Carthusian
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's 4-year-old, freshest runner in the field at just 14 days since last start, with hood fitted; a true prominent type whose five most recent runs show no win on good ground (0W1P), and the form string of 56-707 gives little reason to think the redistribution penalty won't prove decisive here.

races.paceDynamic: Poetic Sound is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her from the front, Colin Keane can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m½f trip on good ground — a tempo that suits her perfectly and gives her every chance to pinch a decisive lead into the straight. Behind her, Robbies Rock, Ballyadam, Carthusian and Happy Jacky are all genuine prominent-running types but with more pace horses than the race shape can accommodate, several will be forced to race in an unfamiliar midfield position rather than their natural slot near the front. The redistribution of those true front-rankers into midfield means the "chasing pack" lacks the authentic hold-up profile to mount a coordinated late challenge, leaving the hold-up horses — Reverend Hubert, Highwind, Cock And Bull — as the only pure closers, though they must hope the pace is genuine enough to bring them into it. This race shape, with a sole uncontested pace-setter and a muddled, congested middle group, strongly favours horses who can track the leader in a true prominent position from the outset and quicken from a close-up spot in the final two furlongs — particularly Delta and Kilmeaden, who are genuine enough in style to secure that berth.

watchPoints.text: Poetic Sound's early control is the race pivot — watch whether Colin Keane takes up the lead immediately or is challenged; if she is left alone in front the race is almost certainly run to her conditions.

Robbies Rock, Ballyadam and Carthusian are all genuine prominent types likely to push forward regardless of their mapped positions — if two or more press to the front aggressively in the first half-mile, the pace could inflate unexpectedly and blow the race wide open.

Reverend Hubert is the most authentic hold-up horse in the race with proven winning form at this track on good ground; watch his position at halfway — if the pace is honest he is the principal late threat to the leader.

Delta's jockey booking (Oisin Murphy, a high-profile international name) is notable for a handicapper in this company — watch for an aggressive early move to track the leader and press from 3f out rather than waiting for an opening.

Hatim and Cock And Bull both carry long-absence flags (227 and 272 days respectively) — their early running style and how quickly they settle will signal whether connections are simply seeking a fitness run or targeting a competitive showing.

races.name: Corinthian Challenge Charity Race Series

runners_data.name: Spinola Bay
runners_data.note: Good record at this trip on Good ground with two recent wins at 16f, and the OR=120 ceiling combined with Gordon Elliott's in-form yard makes this the most natural beneficiary of a prominent position tracking the leader; well-placed from a tactical standpoint.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: Won over 23f on Good recently and has strong placed form at 22f, so the trip and ground suit — but Jack Foley's yard has only one runner in the T14 window and this horse is a natural front-runner that the crowded prominent rank has pushed onto the midfield map, meaning it will need to work to recover its preferred slot.

runners_data.name: Red Hugh O'Donnell
runners_data.note: Dropped significantly in OR to 68 and form figures include a flat zero last time; the horse has moved from sprint distances to 1m4f here which is an unusual profile jump, and its hold-up style means it needs a stronger gallop than this race is likely to produce.

runners_data.name: The Mediator
runners_data.note: Has been placed three times in five recent runs including a win at 16f on Soft, so form and distance fit reasonably well, but this is inherently a horse that wants to race prominently and the congested front group means it is likely to find itself shuffled further back than ideal, hampering its chance regardless of ability.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: Won over 20f and has placed at 19f and 22f, suggesting this 1m4f trip may be on the short side, though the Good going and Curragh setting are positives; was off the track for 27 days after a jumping stint and is another OR=120 type that needs to secure a position near Whatyouwant to be effective.

runners_data.name: Banana Three
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with consistent placed efforts at 16f on Good, suggesting distance and going are squarely in its favour — but this is a horse that wants to be up with the pace and the overcrowded prominent group means it is mapped to midfield against its natural instincts, which is a real tactical handicap.

runners_data.name: Limbocall
runners_data.note: OR=53 with a form string of 4370-0 and all recent runs over 8f — this 1m4f trip is considerably further than anything this horse has tackled in its recent history, and the unclassified style (U) adds uncertainty; only back seven days after last run.

runners_data.name: San Andreas
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 16f on the all-weather and shows genuine hold-up profile, but the Good turf going is uncharted territory given all five recent runs are on Standard surfaces; Joseph Patrick O'Brien has a strong T14 record (10/52) and this is the most interesting switch-surface angle in the race for a genuine closer.

runners_data.name: Typical Thomas
runners_data.note: Two wins from 15 similar-going runs suggests it is effective on Good ground and the 18f trip recently confirms stamina, but a 273-day absence (13 days since a hurdles run) makes fitness the key unknown; the hold-up style needs a proper gallop to fire and this race's controlled pace is a concern.

runners_data.name: Wackestone
runners_data.note: Placed at 16f on Good and ran creditably at 16f on Soft, so the distance and ground profile fit, but a lengthy absence of 426 days (81 days since last hurdle run) and no win on Good are flags; Gordon Elliott's yard is active and the horse has shown enough to be on the shortlist of prominent-style contenders.

runners_data.name: Western Model
runners_data.note: Five placed efforts in fifteen similar-going runs without a win is an honest but winless record; races prominently over staying trips and the 22f-plus experience suggests 1m4f could be on the short side, but the Good ground suits and Andrew Kinirons's yard has had a recent winner.

runners_data.name: Nancee Spain
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Soft and placed twice on Good, so the step up to 1m4f on Good is a logical progression — but this is a true hold-up horse that the map has shifted into a midfield slot because of overcrowding at the rear, meaning its natural patient style is understated in the race shape analysis; 79 days since last run.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: The confirmed sole front-runner in this race, set to lead from the front uncontested on Good ground over 1m4f; won over 25f on Good and has Good-ground form, so stamina is not in doubt, though a 273-day absence (via a hurdle run 13 days ago) introduces a fitness caveat for a horse that needs to sustain it alone from the front.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Has placed twice and won once at 16f on various going types including Good, and returns after 251 days (20 days since last hurdle run) for Gordon Elliott's busy yard; sits naturally prominent and has the distance profile to challenge at this trip if fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Elman
runners_data.note: Form figures of 740-0 with all distance history showing incomplete returns on Soft and Heavy — genuinely unknown quantity on Good turf at 1m4f; Denis Gerard Hogan has a modest T14 record and the 103-day absence (87 days since last hurdle run) adds to the uncertainty around this hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Garnetot
runners_data.note: Placed at 20f on Good and ran consistently around staying trips, so the step back to 1m4f is shorter than its recent form suggests it prefers; hold-up style and headgear flag (hg:t) are notable, and Gordon Elliott's strong yard presence is the main positive with only 13 days since last run.

races.paceDynamic: Whatyouwant is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger for the lead expected to press hard from the outset over 1m4f on Good ground at the Curragh, this race is set up for a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Spinola Bay, Way Down South, Wackestone, Western Model and Playtime will likely track in the prominent positions behind Whatyouwant, creating a settled two-tier procession rather than a contested pace scenario. The lack of genuine pressure on the leader means the tempo is unlikely to be searching enough to collapse the front, and those racing close to Whatyouwant from positions two to five are the primary beneficiaries of this shape. The field carries considerably more prominent-racing types than can physically occupy the front rank — Catalani, Banana Three and The Mediator are all natural prominent horses redistributed into a midfield map position, with Spinola Bay and Way Down South the likeliest to actually secure the early slots behind Whatyouwant given their profile and recent fitness. This race shape clearly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the straight, rather than hold-up types who will need a searching gallop to find gaps late.

scenarios.title: Hold-up horses pounce

scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely late on and true closers benefit from a bunched finish with several prominent horses stopping quickly.

watchPoints.text: Spinola Bay and Way Down South — both OR=120 prominent types with recent form at exactly this trip and going, ideally placed to benefit if they secure an early position directly behind the uncontested Whatyouwant; the race shape is built for them.

Catalani, Banana Three and The Mediator — all three are natural prominent racers redistributed into the midfield map due to a congested front rank; watch in the early stages whether any of them manage to push forward, as recovering their preferred position in a 16-runner field on a turning Curragh track is far from guaranteed.

Whatyouwant's fitness — off the track for 273 days with only a hurdle run 13 days ago as prep; if this horse ties up in the final two furlongs after setting its own pace, it could trigger a scramble for the front and compress the finish dramatically.

San Andreas — the only genuinely unexposed Good-turf mover in the hold-up group, switching from all-weather surfaces; watch whether O'Brien's runner shows any ability to travel on a different surface, as this is the one late-challenge angle with some trainer class behind it.

Typical Thomas — two wins from 15 Good-going runs is the best strike rate among the genuine closers, but 273 days off the track is a serious flag; if it shows early vibrancy in the betting market it could be worth monitoring as a pace-collapse beneficiary.
